8	  Two things surfaced by an adversarially-verified six-front assessment on 2026-07-27

12	  1. THE RATIONAL POINT. references/challenge.lean declares ''Jacobian C'' with NO
13	  rational-point binder. But instHasPicScheme (AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean:316)
14	  makes ''[HasRationalPoint C]'' an ESSENTIAL hypothesis, and correctly so -- without
15	  a section, Pic(C x_k T) / pi_T^* Pic(T) need not even be a Zariski sheaf. Kleiman''s
16	  theorem needs no section because it represents the ETALE sheaf. This was assumed
17	  to be a platform limitation; it is not. Mathlib v4.31 does carry the etale topology
18	  (.lake-packages/mathlib/Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Etale.lean:32-50). So it
19	  is a design choice, and as the tree stands the project would prove something strictly
20	  weaker than the challenge asks. Either etale-sheafify the Picard functor, or accept
21	  the weaker theorem and say so. Nothing above this on the Picard path is safe until
22	  it is settled. Roadmap node AJC.picrep.rational-point.
23	
24	
25	  2. THE BLUEPRINT ADVERTISES A ROUTE THE TREE ABANDONED. informal/pic-representability-campaign.md
26	  (2026-07-09) selected route D3 Milne-Kollar -- section trick on the Div substrate,
27	  finite Galois quotient, coproduct assembly -- and states verbatim ''Off-path and
28	  untouched: Quot-lane sorries''. FGAPicRepresentability.lean:550 marks HasSmoothProperQuotient

32	  cost is small -- only QuotRepresentability.lean (83 lines) and SerreFiniteness.lean
33	  (292) are exclusive to the Quot endgame; the other ~9k lines are imported by the
34	  committed route and must NOT be deleted. Decide: re-aim the blueprint and roadmap

36

40	  all of cluster J, the actual Milne construction of Pic^r. Estimate 27k-45k new lines,

49	  would.
